text:
Seth Jarvis missed the start of the season after shoulder surgery and has been back for 10 games. The return has been quiet in the best way: 9 points (2 goals, 7 assists), and Carolina takes 63.4% of the expected goals at five on five when he plays.

He is not yet the player who scored 32 goals last season. He has 2 goals on 2.6 expected, no power-play points, and he is playing 16 minutes a night. None of that is luck in either direction; his finishing and his teammates' are both close to their chances. It looks like a player finding his legs on a deep team.

The underlying game is intact. Evolving-Hockey had him 42nd among forwards in wins above replacement last season, and he drew more penalties than he took. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 86th percentile for chances from in front of the net, with more shots off passes across the slot or from behind the net than most.

Our projection has him finishing between 17 and 31 goals, 23 in the middle. What to watch: his minutes and a return to the power play.
